speech:
I interpret the decision as permission for a bounded simulator exercise, with independent-diagnosis readiness still unknown. My safety authority is joint with yours and does not extend to real-utility certification.

Three constraints matter. C-S1 says we can safely simulate sensor staleness and record a local console log, but the radio-link module cannot inject partial dropouts this week. C-S2 requires both operator and safety approval, and either of us can stop a scenario. C-S3 says the offline paper alarm sheet contains last-known values without automatic freshness marking. I therefore cannot treat that sheet as an automatically current fallback or claim that a rehearsal covers partial radio dropouts.

I propose withholding release now while we prepare one bounded package: a timestamp job aid for 1 unit, stop-and-handoff procedure for 2, and a sensor-staleness fault rehearsal with local incident logging for 3. A learning-scientist consultation costs 1, bringing the proposal to 7 of 8 units. No separate unranked practice or delayed probe is included. My proposed release conditions are a demonstrated freshness check, an observable stop and handoff when freshness cannot be established, and our explicit joint approval; partial radio dropout coverage remains excluded and unverified.

Operator, can you describe the handoff and freshness-check steps your team could actually carry out within this scope, including who receives a stopped scenario? I request the scientist's advice on what, if anything, the supplied acknowledgement-time improvement establishes about independent diagnosis, and what limitations we must retain without a delayed probe.
